title: Pull-cord start: a 2-pin header whose START pin a cord's wire loop holds low; the firmware starts when it is pulled and stops after the match
circuit: START (pin 1) on a GPIO, pulled up 10 kOhm to 3V3 (circuit.ts supportParts); GND on pin 2. The cord ends in a 2-way 2.54 mm socket with a wire loop: in, START reads low; pulled, it reads high. The header has no latch, so the socket comes away with the cord.
checks: mechanics/safety.ts startChecks: the plug on a board, START on a GPIO at its pin. Firmware (templates/fw-rover/src/match.h, host-tested in test/test_match): arms only after seeing the cord in, starts once it has stayed out 50 ms, stops every motor MATCH_MS after the start (mechanics.safety.start.matchS) and never restarts until reset.

rules.rule: Eurobot General Rules 1.2, F.6 Starting cord
rules.where: p. 13: started by pulling a cord at least 500 mm long that must not stay attached; no other start (remote, switch) is homologated

rules.rule: Eurobot General Rules 1.2, H.3 End of match
rules.where: p. 20: at the end of the 100 seconds the robots must stop and turn off all their actuators

open: The cord itself (at least 500 mm, the rule check's figure) and its socket are the team's: no catalog entry. Actuators a team adds besides the drive motors must check the match too (main.cpp gates only the drive).
